entry.title: Turning Plant Waste Into Products, Recycling Waste Heat, and a New Battery Manufacturing Consortium

media:group.media:title: Turning Plant Waste Into Products, Recycling Waste Heat, and a New Battery Manufacturing Consortium
media:group.media:description:
At the National Laboratory of the Rockies, collaboration and partnerships go hand in hand with research. Today, two startups in the Shell GameChanger Accelerator Powered by NLR program are working to turn plant waste into products. And the latest iteration of the URBANopt tool is helping city planners recycle waste heat—and save money—in neighborhoods. Then, NLR and other national labs join the Department of Energy’s Battery Manufacturing Consortium, also called BattMan.

entry.title: Alaska's Future: How a National Lab Is Powering Critical Minerals

media:group.media:title: Alaska's Future: How a National Lab Is Powering Critical Minerals
media:group.media:description:
Alaska's critical minerals could power America's energy future — but unlocking them takes affordable energy and infrastructure for remote mining operations.
In August 2026, the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) hosted the Alaska Mining Energy & Infrastructure Workshop in Fairbanks, bringing together mining operators, researchers, utilities, government representatives, and other stakeholders to tackle shared challenges and explore technical innovation and collaboration.
From improving energy affordability and reliability to addressing infrastructure needs in remote Arctic environments, the conversations focused on connecting industry experience with research capabilities to find practical, deployable solutions.
Hear perspectives from Alaska's mining industry, NLR researchers, and the University of Alaska Fairbanks on the challenges, opportunities, and partnerships that could shape the state's energy and critical minerals future.
Learn more about working with NLR: https://www.nlr.gov/workingwithus

entry.title: Energy Modeling, a Collegiate Competition, and Amorphous Materials

media:group.media:title: Energy Modeling, a Collegiate Competition, and Amorphous Materials
media:group.media:description:
New tools, discoveries, and solutions are happening every day at the National Laboratory of the Rockies. Today, a newly released software is helping architects and engineers model building energy use without needing to learn computer programming language. And universities across the country are competing in the Technology Recycling and Repurposing (T-ReX) Collegiate Competition to find new uses for retired energy technologies. Then, researchers at NLR and the Colorado School of Mines use quantum mechanics to better understand the materials underpinning modern electronics.

entry.title: Putting Marine Energy Tech to the Test

media:group.media:title: Putting Marine Energy Tech to the Test
media:group.media:description:
Need a facility to test your marine energy technology? Partner with NLR through TEAMER to access world-class testing and expertise. TEAMER — Testing Expertise and Access for Marine Energy Research — connects developers with the nation's leading test facilities, labs, and experts to accelerate wave energy, tidal energy, and ocean energy technologies from concept to deployment. Whether you're validating a wave energy converter prototype, de-risking a tidal system, or scaling toward commercialization, NLR can help you find the right test site, technical support, and funding pathway.
Learn more at https://teamer-us.org/

media:group.media:description:

entry.title: Lab Notes: The Advanced Research on Integrated Energy Systems (ARIES) Platform

media:group.media:title: Lab Notes: The Advanced Research on Integrated Energy Systems (ARIES) Platform
media:group.media:description:
In this Lab Notes episode, hosts Kerrin and Taylor explore NLR's Advanced Research on Integrated Energy Systems (https://www.nlr.gov/aries) , or ARIES platform. ARIES is a first-of-its-kind research platform that uses innovative capabilities to help us find solutions for the grid of the future.
Learn about its history, what it actually does, and how this work can contribute to a more affordable, reliable, and secure energy future. Hear from leading ARIES experts and take a look at one ARIES project called SuperLab, which demonstrates how we can connect energy assets and sources from differing locations and get them to work together seamlessly as one balanced energy system.

entry.title: REORG Controls Create Cellular, Not Centralized, Power Grid Resilience

media:group.media:title: REORG Controls Create Cellular, Not Centralized, Power Grid Resilience
media:group.media:description: The REORG solution was developed through a U.S. Department of Energy effort to use distributed grid resources for faster recovery and adaptive resilience. The effort resulted in a control architecture that was demonstrated in Western Colorado where wildfires and landslides can isolate communities from power supply, and where a more cellular approach could add resilience by relying on local resources.

entry.title: Testing a Tidal Energy Blade to the Breaking Point

media:group.media:title: Testing a Tidal Energy Blade to the Breaking Point
media:group.media:description:
How much pressure can a tidal energy blade take? NLR can help find the answer.
NLR is leading the way in materials testing. With low-cost tests like these, NLR offers cost and time savings for manufacturers by ensuring that their materials can withstand their intended environments. NLR’s materials testing allows manufacturers to validate their designs and materials prior to deployment, accelerating the ability to confidently release these materials in real-world scenarios.
Learn more at: https://www.nlr.gov/manufacturing/marine-energy https://www.energy.gov/cmei/water/us-testing-expertise-and-access-marine-energy-research-program-teamer
